Title: Standardize destructive-action confirmation and recovery across workbenches
Description:
Problem: the 2026-05-25 modal-flow review found inconsistent destructive-action handling. Chat delete uses a native browser confirmation, but Pages delete, Memories delete, Profile sign-in method removal, and Admin model profile deletion call their delete/remove services directly from UI handlers. Some edit-buffer removals such as tag namespace rows and variable rows are less risky because they still require a later save, but persisted deletes/removals need a consistent confirmation and recovery story.

Desired outcome: destructive actions should require intentional confirmation, explain what will be removed, and provide a recoverability path where the backing store supports it.

Scope:
- In scope: Page delete, Memory delete, Chat delete, Profile sign-in method removal, Admin model profile deletion, confirmation copy, cancel/default focus behavior, snackbar/undo or history recovery affordances, and browser coverage for cancel/confirm paths.
- Out of scope: changing persistence semantics for soft-delete/history unless needed to expose an existing recovery path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Persisted destructive actions use a consistent app-level confirmation dialog rather than silent execution or native browser-only prompts.
- Confirmation copy includes the affected item type/name and whether the action is recoverable.
- Cancel is the safe default and keyboard/focus behavior is accessible.
- Success/failure feedback explains what changed and, where practical, links to history or provides undo.

Validation:
- Run focused browser checks for canceling and confirming page, memory, chat, profile-link, and model-profile destructive actions using safe fixtures.
- Confirm no live production wiki records or account links are mutated during review/validation without fixture isolation.

Imported from Data/Pages/workbench/tasks.md; broadened with live/code evidence on 2026-05-25.

Comments.Author: tracker-import
Comments.Body: Keep notes on the exact confirmation copy and whether the action feels recoverable.

Comments.Author: AgentSmith
Comments.Body: Review update: code inspection found direct persisted deletes/removals in Pages, Memories, Profile sign-in methods, and Admin model profiles, while Chat uses a native confirm. Broadened this task to standardize confirmation/recovery across destructive actions.

Comments.Author: AgentSmith
Comments.Body: Implemented a shared MudBlazor destructive-action confirmation helper and routed persisted Page delete, Memory delete, Chat session delete, Profile sign-in method removal, and Admin model profile deletion through it. Confirmation copy names the affected item and describes recovery/irreversibility, cancel/close/escape keep the current state, Chat no longer uses native `confirm` for delete, and success feedback now calls out deletion/recovery where applicable. Also excluded nested `artifacts/**` validation outputs from App/Core project default compile globs after generated validation obj files broke local builds. Validation: `dotnet build .\MemorySmith.App\MemorySmith.App.csproj --nologo` succeeded; `MEMORYSMITH_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5099 npm run test:route-smoke` passed 5/5 with a disposable localStorage Chat delete-cancel browser check; static handler sweep confirmed the five persisted destructive mutations now call `ConfirmDestructiveActionAsync`. Authenticated Page/Memory/Profile/Admin confirm-path clicks were not run against live project data to avoid mutating production wiki/account records without fixture-isolated app startup.
